scope: Source investigation/TDD only after the 837e7997 local load; no new shipping-image/hour or existing-Demo acceptance.
findings: All seven soak probe failures are socket timeouts, not HTTP503.
Six episodes have an engine loop sample in libpq I/O within or adjacent to the probe request; one samples executor PnL computation. Sampling does not explain every millisecond.

No selected GC interval is captured for these episodes. Five of seven sampled context intervals have no additional cgroup throttling; the other increments are small. This does not exclude host scheduling or prove one exclusive cause.

Healthy created-order counts are identical across both runs; increased quote count does not explain the probe count difference. Host conditions, scheduling and Random trajectories were not replay-controlled.

The fresh ownership SELECT previously opened a read transaction and waited on COMMIT. A scoped Psycopg autocommit flag preserves the same backend/advisory-lock checks and unchanged SQLAlchemy isolation metadata, restores transaction mode, and registers no pool-reset callbacks. No authority cache or probe budget change.
Teardown of a closed/invalidated owner now closes without reconnecting or attempting a new-session write.
Already-open SQLAlchemy or direct DBAPI read transactions retain their original check/commit behavior. Idle reads use scoped driver autocommit; write isolation and client deadlines are unchanged.

targeted_component.scope: Warmed native recorder-owner fixture on real PostgreSQL; no whole-engine/probe latency claim.

controlled_probe.scope: Real local PostgreSQL owner and production health/probe functions; controlled COMMIT jitter, not a full MM or historical-cause proof.

invalid_draft.note: One first-draft test used nonexistent store.load; corrected to read before the valid Red run. Not runtime-defect proof.

intermediate_failure.note: Read scope passed; release of the closed connection raised ResourceClosedError. Resolved with explicit no-reconnect teardown; retained failure.

mode_restore_red.reason: A plain SQLAlchemy close returned the mode-uncertain live DBAPI connection to its pool. Corrected to invalidate/discard before closing.

io_deadline_closed_state.note: Original 3s deadline passed, but the old assertion required invalidated=True; permanent close sets that False. Owner now requires physical closure and permanent logical closure; other modes retain invalidation checks.

superseded_bounded_regression.note: Intentionally interrupted after the permanent-closure assertion failure; final compatibility/cleanup checks and frozen regressions supersede it.

qualifications: A matched controlled read-COMMIT fault establishes that mechanism, not the unique cause of seven older production-style episodes.
The controlled app uses the real health/probe functions and real PostgreSQL ownership, but does not run a full market-making strategy.
Component timings use a native local process and a real disposable PostgreSQL server; no whole-image/p99 speedup is claimed.
Source changes do not inherit the accepted 837e7997 image hour gate.
Reported read timing medians are over seven 25-read batch means, not individual-request p50/tail or a whole-engine benchmark.

rejected_prototype.issue: Changing isolation through execution_options appends connection pool-return reset callbacks for each change.
